title: Chapter 60: Sandu: The Three Poisons 5
content:
Chapter 60

Wen Ning summoned dozens of disciples, personally escorting them to a lavish, sprawling estate. Slipping in through the back gate, he led Wei Wuxian into a secluded side chamber.

Yet the moment Wen Ning turned to latch the door behind them, before he could even catch his breath, Wei Wuxian’s hand shot out, pinning him by the throat.

"What is this place?!" Wei Wuxian demanded in a harsh, venomous whisper.

Even though Wen Ning had just saved their necks, Wei Wuxian wasn't about to drop his guard around someone wearing Wen colors; every nerve was on high alert. Navigating the estate’s corridors just now, they’d passed countless rooms buzzing with harsh Qishan accents. Stray words drifting through the cracked windows and door seams hadn't slipped past his ears, and among the scattered chatter, one chilling term had stood out like a sore thumb:Supervisory Office!

Wen Ning flailed his hands in a frantic panic. "No... I..."

"No what?!" Wei Wuxian snarled. "Isn't this the Supervisory Office set up right here in Yiling? Which poor, ruined clan’s ancestral home did your family steal this time? What the hell are you playing at, dragging us in here?"

Wen Ning scrambled to explain, breathless and desperate. "Wei-gongzi, p-please listen to me! Yes, it’s a Supervisory Office! But... but I swear on my life I'm not trying to hurt you! If I wanted you dead, I could've backed out the second I walked into Lotus Pier last night. Why would I bother sneaking you all the way here?"

Wei Wuxian’s nerves had been stretched to the absolute breaking point for days, raw, frayed, and ready to snap at the slightest spark. His skull throbbed with exhaustion, and hearing this barely chipped away at his suspicion.

Wen Ning pressed on, "Thisisa Supervisory Office, which means it's the one place on earth the Wen Clan will never bother to search. You can hide here safely. Just... please, whatever you do, don't let anyone spot you..."

After a tense, agonizing beat, Wei Wuxian forced his white-knuckled fingers to uncoil. Muttering a rough, reluctant "Thank you, and sorry," he turned away, gently laying Jiang Cheng flat on the wooden daybed.

Before he could pull his hands back, the door flew open. A sharp, imperious female voice rang out: "I was looking for you! You'd better explain yourself right now—"

Don't let anyone spot you, and within five seconds, they were busted.

A cold sweat broke across Wei Wuxian’s spine as he pivoted instantly, putting his own body between the door and the daybed. Wen Ning froze, completely struck dumb with terror.

The two of them locked eyes with the young woman standing in the doorway. She had a sun-kissed, slightly dusky complexion and striking, sweet features, offset by a gaze dripping with haughty, effortless arrogance. Across her sunburst robes, the scarlet flames burned with an eye-searing, brilliant intensity, flickering vividly along her collar and wide sleeves.

Her rank was terrifyingly high—on equal footing with Wen Chao himself!

For a suffocating few seconds, the room hung in a dead, frozen standoff. Outside, a flurry of hurried footsteps approached down the hall. Steeling himself for a bloodbath, Wei Wuxian tensed to strike—only for the girl to beat him to the punch. With a sharp flick of her wrist, she slammed the door shut.

A muffled voice called from the other side, "Office Master Wen, is something wrong?"

Her reply was cool, smooth, and utterly bored. "Nothing. My useless brother is back, wilting like a bruised cabbage again. Don't bother him. Let's go finish our discussion."

The retainers mumbled their compliance, their footsteps fading down the corridor alongside hers. Wen Ning let out a ragged breath, turning to Wei Wuxian with an awkward, timid whisper: "M-My... my sister."

Wei Wuxian’s brows shot up. "Wen Qing is your sister?"

Wen Ning gave an embarrassed, sheepish nod. "My sister. She's... very impressive."

'Impressive' was putting it lightly.

Wen Qing was practically a celebrity within the Qishan Wen Sect. While not a direct daughter of Sect Leader Wen Ruohan, she was the descendant of one of his cousins. Though distant on paper, Wen Ruohan had grown up close with that cousin. Coupled with her brilliant intellect, formidable cultivation, and peerless mastery of medicine, she had earned Wen Ruohan’s deep favor. She routinely sat at his side during grand banquets hosted by Qishan Wen, which was why Wei Wuxian vaguely remembered her face—she was hard to miss, being quite the looker. He’d also heard faint whispers that she had a sibling, but because the brother was thoroughly eclipsed by her brilliance, nobody ever bothered talking about him.

Wei Wuxian stared in genuine disbelief. "You're seriously her brother?"

Assuming Wei Wuxian was marveling at how such an extraordinary, celebrated woman could have such an unremarkable, pathetic brother, Wen Ning ducked his head. "Yeah. My sister is incredible. I'm... not."

"No, no, that's not what I meant," Wei Wuxian corrected hastily. "You're great too. What blows my mind is that your sister is Wen Qing, an actual Office Master, and you still had the guts to smuggle us..."

A faint rustle from the daybed cut him off. Jiang Cheng shifted, his brow twitching into a slight furrow. Wei Wuxian whirled around instantly. "Jiang Cheng?!"

Wen Ning scrambled toward the exit. "He's awake! He needs medicine—I'll go brew it right now."

He slipped through the door, clicking it shut behind him. After days of comatose delirium, Jiang Cheng’s eyelids fluttered open, drifting back to consciousness. A wave of ecstatic relief washed over Wei Wuxian, but within a heartbeat, that joy curdled into unease.

Something was deeply, terribly wrong.

Jiang Cheng’s expression was bizarre. It was quiet—far too quiet, flat as stagnant water.

He simply stared blankly at the ceiling timbers, utterly numb, showing zero curiosity about where he was or what had become of him.

Wei Wuxian hadn't braced for this reaction. No tears, no fury, no panic—just absolute, hollow nothingness. His stomach plummeted. "Jiang Cheng? Can you see me? Can you hear me? Do you know who I am?"

Jiang Cheng’s eyes slid over to him, cold and mute. Wei Wuxian bombarded him with frantic questions until, finally, Jiang Cheng braced his elbows against the mattress and dragged himself upright. Looking down at the jagged, weeping scar from the Discipline Whip slashed across his chest, his lips curled into a mocking, empty sneer.

Once the mark of a Discipline Whip bit into flesh, that brand of humiliation was etched into bone forever. Wei Wuxian swallowed his own dread, forcing out a hollow lie: "Don't look at it. We'll find a way to clear it up."

Jiang Cheng raised a hand and struck him across the chest. The blow was entirely limp, lacking even the force of a gentle breeze. Wei Wuxian didn't budge an inch. "Hit me," he murmured quietly. "Hit me as much as you want, if it makes you feel better."

Jiang Cheng asked, his voice dead, "Did you feel that?"

Wei Wuxian blinked. "Feel what?"

"Did you feel my spiritual energy?"

Wei Wuxian frowned. "What spiritual energy? You didn't use any."

"I did."

Wei Wuxian’s throat went dry. "What are you... what are you talking about?"

Jiang Cheng repeated, spitting out every syllable with chilling precision: "I said, I used it. That strike just now—I poured every shred of spiritual power in my core into it. Now answer me: did you feel it?"

Wei Wuxian stared at him, blood draining from his face. After a suffocating silence, he managed, "Hit me again. Try one more time."

"There's no point," Jiang Cheng whispered, dead-eyed. "Hit you a hundred times, and it'll be the exact same result. Wei Wuxian... do you know why the Core-Melting Hand is called what he is?"

Wei Wuxian’s heart plummeted straight through the floorboards.

Jiang Cheng continued in a hollow monotone, "Because those palms of his can dissolve a golden core, ensuring the victim can never form another. The spiritual energy shatters and bleeds away, reducing you to an ordinary mortal.

"And an ordinary mortal in a cultivation clan is nothing more than a useless cripple. Destined to crawl through the dirt, never able to dream of touching a sword again.

"My mother and father... Wen Zhuliu melted their golden cores first. Stripped them of every ounce of resistance, and only then did he butcher them."

Wei Wuxian’s mind spun into a chaotic void of sheer panic. He stumbled backward, trembling, muttering numbly, "...The Core-Melting Hand... the Core-Melting Hand..."

Jiang Cheng let out a broken, derisive laugh. "Wen Zhuliu... Wen Zhuliu! I want vengeance! I want to tear them to pieces! But how?! How the hell am I supposed to get revenge?! I don't have a golden core anymore! I can't ever cultivate again! What am I supposed to fight them with?! Hahaha... hahahaha!"

Wei Wuxian collapsed onto the floor, staring up at the unraveling boy, utterly paralyzed. Words completely failed him.

No one in the world understood better than Wei Wuxian how fiercely proud Jiang Cheng was, how desperately he clung to his cultivation and spiritual standing. And now, a single strike from the Core-Melting Hand had pulverized his cultivation, his pride, and his final hope for vengeance into absolute dust!

Jiang Cheng laughed like a raving madman, tossing his head back until he flopped flat on the bed, splaying his arms out in sheer, broken surrender. "Wei Wuxian, why the hell did you bother saving me?! What good is dragging me out alive?! So I can sit here like a helpless worm, watching those Wen dogs strut across our home while I rot into nothing?!"

Right on cue, the door creaked open, and Wen Ning stepped inside. Wearing an anxious, almost timidly appeasing smile, he carefully carried a steaming bowl of black medicinal broth toward the bed. Before he could speak a word, the brilliant sunburst embroidery caught Jiang Cheng's eye, and his pupils contracted into pinpricks.

Jiang Cheng lashed out with a vicious kick! The blow struck Wen Ning square in the chest, flipping the bowl and sending the scalding, dark broth splashing across his robes. Wei Wuxian lunged to catch the falling porcelain, instinctively reaching out to steady the shell-shocked Wen Ning.

Jiang Cheng’s roar shook the walls: "What is wrong with you?!"

Wen Ning scrambled backward in terror as Jiang Cheng snatched Wei Wuxian’s lapels, screaming into his face, "A Wen dog stands right in front of you, and you don't cut his throat?! You're actually holding him up?! Do you have a death wish?!"

Even pouring every ounce of frantic fury into his grip, his fingers were hopelessly weak, and Wei Wuxian broke the hold with effortless ease. Only then did Jiang Cheng seem to register his surroundings, his bloodshot eyes darting around the unfamiliar room. "Where are we?"

From across the room, Wen Ning squeaked, "The Yiling Supervisory Office... but it's really sa—"

Jiang Cheng whipped around, glaring daggers at Wei Wuxian. "A Supervisory Office?! You walked us right into their trap?!"

"No, that's not it!" Wei Wuxian shouted.

"Not it?!" Jiang Cheng snarled, his voice cracking. "Then what are you doing inside a Wen outpost?! How did you get here?! Don't you dare tell me you begged those Wen dogs for help!"

Wei Wuxian grabbed his arms, desperate to ground him. "Jiang Cheng, calm down! We're safe here! Pull yourself together—the Core-Melting Hand might not be entirely irreversible..."

Jiang Cheng was completely past the point of reason, teetering on the edge of utter psychosis. Clamping his hands around Wei Wuxian’s throat, he broke into wild, hysterical laughter: "Wei Wuxian... Hahahahaha! Wei Wuxian! You... you..."

Suddenly, a flash of crimson kicked the door off its latch, and a figure blurred into the room. A silver glint cleaved the air, and a needle plunged straight into Jiang Cheng’s scalp; his eyes rolled back, and he dropped limply onto the mattress. Wen Qing whirled around, slamming the door shut with a furious hiss: "Wen Ning, are you out of your mind?! Letting him scream and laugh at the top of his lungs?! Are you trying to get us caught?!"

Seeing her, Wen Ning latched on like a drowning man to a raft. "Jiejie!"

"Don't you 'Jiejie' me!" Wen Qing snapped, turning her wrath on him. "When did you grow the spine to pull a stunt this reckless?! Hiding fugitives?! I already made discreet inquiries—no wonder you suddenly bolted for Yunmeng! What gave you the suicidal audacity to pull this off?! If Wen Chao finds out, he'll flay you alive! If he decides he wants someone dead, do you honestly think I have the power to stop him?!"

Her words rattled off like rapid-fire arrows, sharp, articulate, and brooking zero defiance. Wei Wuxian couldn't find an opening to squeeze a single syllable in.

Wen Ning turned pale as paper. "Jiejie, but Wei-gongzi..."

"I know you did this out of some misplaced sense of gratitude, so I'll hold my tongue on that," she cut in sharply. "But these two cannot stay here! You vanish and pop back up right as Wen Chao loses his high-value prisoner—do you think Wen Chao is completely braindead? They'll trace the trail here sooner or later. This is my Supervisory Office, and this is your bedroom; do you have any idea what the punishment is if you're caught harboring them? Use your head!"

She laid out the stakes with brutal clarity, stopping just short of pointing at Wei Wuxian’s nose and telling them to get the hell out so they wouldn't drag her house down with them. If Wei Wuxian were the only one wounded, or if their savior had been anyone else, his pride would have demanded he bid them farewell and walk out the door that very second. But Jiang Cheng was the one lying on that bed—broken, coreless, his sanity hanging by a thread. He couldn't afford to be proud. And beneath the shame, a bitter injustice burned: the Wen Clan was the sole reason they were reduced to this misery in the first place. Wei Wuxian could only grit his teeth in suffocating silence.

Wen Ning mumbled, "B-But... it was the Wen Clan who..."

"The crimes of the Wen Clan are not my crimes, and their blood debts are not mine to pay!" Wen Qing cut him off, her dark eyes flashing toward Wei Wuxian. "Don't look at me like that, Wei Ying. Every debt has its debtor. I may be the Office Master of Yiling, but I took this post under direct orders. I am a physician and an apothecary; I have never taken a single life, and not a single drop of your Jiang Clan's blood stains my hands!"

It was the unvarnished truth. In all his years, Wei Wuxian had never heard of Wen Qing causing a single death or orchestrating any atrocities; if anything, branches practically begged for her to oversee their territories. She was one of the few sane, honorable souls in her entire bloodline, occasionally even putting in a good word before Wen Ruohan to temper his cruelty. Her reputation had always been immaculate.

Silence fell heavy over the room.

After an agonizing pause, Wen Qing exhaled. "Leave that needle in his head. The second that kid wakes up, he'll start screaming again, and the whole courtyard will hear him. Pull it out only once his physical wounds have healed, and then get the hell out. I have zero interest in dealing with Wen Chao, and that little concubine of his makes me sick to my stomach!"

With that, she swept out the door.

Wei Wuxian blinked. "Did she... did she just say we can't stay long, but we can hold out here for a few days?"

Wen Ning nodded eagerly, calling out into the hall, "Thank you, Jiejie!"

A pouch of wrapped herbs came flying through the open doorway, smacking Wen Ning square in the chest. Wen Qing’s voice drifted back from down the hall: "If you actually want to thank me, grow a spine! What kind of foul sludge were you brewing just now? Do it over!"

Taking the blow with a grin, Wen Ning clutched the pouch like a treasure. "My sister’s formulas are the best. A hundred times better than mine. Guaranteed."

The boulder crushing Wei Wuxian’s chest finally lifted. "Thank you."

He knew full well that this pair of siblings—one turning a blind eye, the other actively breaking every rule to save them—were staking their lives on the line. Just as Wen Qing had said, if Wen Chao set his sights on someone, she wouldn't be able to protect them, and her own branch would be dragged into the slaughter. Blood relatives from an offshoot family would never carry the weight of the main line.

With the silver needle pinned in his acupoints, Jiang Cheng slept for three days straight. His fractured ribs and lacerations knit back together, leaving behind only the indelible scar of the Discipline Whip, and the hollow void where his golden core had once rested—injuries that would never mend.

And for those three days, Wei Wuxian thought until his head burned.

On the fourth day, Wei Wuxian bid Wen Ning farewell. Carrying Jiang Cheng on his back, they hiked deep into the woods, borrowing an empty shack from an old forester.

Once the door was barred, he pulled the silver needle from Jiang Cheng’s scalp. It took a long time for Jiang Cheng’s lashes to flutter open.

He was awake, but entirely lifeless. He didn't turn over, nor did he muster the energy to ask where they were. He refused water, turned away food, waiting purely for death to claim him.

Wei Wuxian broke the silence. "Do you really want to die?"

Jiang Cheng stared blankly at the wall. "Alive, I can't take revenge. Better to die—maybe I'll return as a fierce ghost."

"You went through the Soul-Calming Rites as an infant," Wei Wuxian said flatly. "You won't turn into a fierce ghost after death."

"If I can't take revenge whether I'm dead or alive, what difference does it make?"

With that, his lips sealed shut, refusing to utter another syllable.

Wei Wuxian sat on the edge of the mattress, watching him in silence for a long time. Finally, he patted his knees, stood up, and busied himself around the shack.

By dusk, he set a steaming meal on the table. "Get up. Eat."

Predictably, Jiang Cheng didn't twitch. Wei Wuxian sat down, picking up his chopsticks. "If you don't keep your strength up, how are you going to reclaim your golden core?"

At the wordsgolden core, Jiang Cheng’s eyes flickered.

Wei Wuxian continued evenly, "You heard me right. I said:reclaim your golden core."

Jiang Cheng’s lips parted, his voice raspy as grinding stones. "...You have a way?"

"I do," Wei Wuxian said, leaning forward. "You've known for years that my mother, Cangse Sanren, was the disciple of Baoshan Sanren, haven't you?"

Those few words hit Jiang Cheng like a bolt of lightning, reigniting a blaze behind his hollow eyes.

Baoshan Sanren—the legendary immortal said to have lived for hundreds of years, an untouchable sage capable of raising the dead and mending shattered bones!

His voice trembled violently. "You mean... you mean..."

Wei Wuxian articulated every syllable with absolute calm: "I mean, I know which mountain she embraces. I can take you to find Baoshan Sanren."

Jiang Cheng stammered, "...B-But didn't you say you couldn't remember your childhood?!"

"I don't remember all of it," Wei Wuxian explained smoothly. "But fragments that were drilled into my head over and over? Those, I never forgot. I distinctly remember a woman's voice repeating a location and a set of instructions. She told me that if I ever found myself backed into a corner with nowhere left to turn, I could go to that mountain and beg the immortal for aid."

Jiang Cheng rolled clean out of bed.

Scrambling across the floorboards to the table, he reached out, but Wei Wuxian pushed the bowl and chopsticks into his hands. "Eat."

Clutching the edge of the wood, Jiang Cheng shook. "I..."

"Eat," Wei Wuxian cut him off firmly. "We talk while you eat, or we don't talk at all."

Jiang Cheng hauled himself onto a stool, frantically shoveling rice into his mouth. From the depths of despair to blinding hope, the whiplash had him burning up inside, fidgeting so violently he didn't even notice he was holding his chopsticks upside down. Watching him chew, Wei Wuxian said, "I'll take you there in a few days."

Jiang Cheng choked, "Today!"

"What are you panicking for?" Wei Wuxian chided gently. "An immortal who's lived for centuries isn't going to vanish into thin air in a few days. We wait because there are strict taboos involved, and I need to drill every rule into your head. Break a single restriction and offend Grandmaster, and we're both finished."

Jiang Cheng stared at him, hanging onto every breath.

"Once you set foot on that mountain," Wei Wuxian warned, "you cannot open your eyes to look around, you cannot memorize the paths, and you cannot look at anyone's face. Whatever they tell you to do, obey without question."

"Understood!"

"And the most important rule of all: if they ask who you are, you must swear that you are Cangse Sanren's son! Do not let your real identity slip under any circumstances!"

"Understood!"

At this point, if Wei Wuxian told him to walk through fire, Jiang Cheng would have nodded with bloodshot eyes.

Wei Wuxian patted his shoulder. "Good. Eat up, build your strength, and rest. I have preparations to make over the next few days."

Jiang Cheng finally realized his chopsticks were backward, flipped them around, and took a massive bite. The blistering spice brought tears to his eyes, but he couldn't help muttering through a cough, "...Tastes terrible!"

After enduring days of relentless grilling about every minute detail regarding Baoshan Sanren, Wei Wuxian finally led Jiang Cheng out, trekking through the wilderness until they reached the foot of a remote mountain in Yiling.

The peak was lush and emerald, wrapped in swirling banks of celestial mist—it certainly carried an otherworldly, ethereal charm. Still, it fell a bit short of the divine paradise legends spoke of. Jiang Cheng had spent the entire journey oscillating between manic hope and paranoid dread—one second suspecting Wei Wuxian was pulling his leg, the next worrying Wei Wuxian had misremembered his childhood memories, and terrified they’d find nothing at all. Staring at the misty peak, his doubts flared again. "Is this really where Baoshan Sanren resides?"

Wei Wuxian’s tone was absolute rock. "Without a doubt. What would I gain by lying to you? Giving you false hope just to crush you harder later?"

It was an exchange they had repeated a hundred times. Escorting him halfway up the winding trail, Wei Wuxian halted. "Alright. From here, I can't go any further."

Pulling out a black strip of cloth, he tied it securely over Jiang Cheng’s eyes, whispering fierce reminders: "Whatever you do, do not take this blindfold off. There are no wild beasts up there, so take it slow; even if you trip, do not touch the cloth. Keep your curiosity dead. Remember: you are Wei Wuxian. You know how to answer their questions, right?"

With his golden core and the blood debt of his entire clan hanging in the balance, Jiang Cheng didn't dare falter, nodding with dead seriousness.

He turned and began his slow, blind ascent up the misty path. Wei Wuxian called after him, "I'll wait for you in that town below!"

Watching Jiang Cheng’s silhouette slowly vanish into the mountain fog, Wei Wuxian turned around, taking a completely different path down the slopes.

Jiang Cheng was gone for seven whole days.

The desolate little border town they’d chosen as their rendezvous point was tucked deep within the valleys, home to barely a handful of souls. The dirt roads were narrow, rutted, and empty of even a passing peddler.

Wei Wuxian squatted by the ditch, staring toward the peaks. Still no sign of Jiang Cheng. Bracing his hands against his knees, he pushed himself up, only for a wave of vertigo to wash over his brain, his footing wobbling unsteadily. Steadying his breath, he trudged toward the lone teahouse in town.

The teahouse was the only structure around that didn't look like a ramshackle shack. The second he crossed the threshold, a waiter beamed, rushing over with an eager grin. "What can I get you, sir?"

Wei Wuxian’s gut instantly clenched.

After days of relentless physical strain without a second to wash, he looked practically like a vagrant. An ordinary teahouse attendant seeing someone in his state would have scowled and kicked him to the curb; this level of fawning enthusiasm was entirely unnatural.

His eyes swept the room in a split-second scan. Behind the counter, the bookkeeper’s head was buried so deep into his ledger he might as well have been wearing it. Across the ten tables, seven or eight patrons sat scattered in silence, cloaked in heavy travel mantles with their hoods drawn low over their tea bowls, clearly concealing their robes.

Wei Wuxian spun on his heel to bolt!

Before his boot could clear the doorframe, a massive, looming shadow cut off the light, and a concussive, thunderous palm slammed straight into his sternum!

The impact blasted Wei Wuxian backward, shattering two wooden tables to splinters. The waiter and bookkeeper scrambled out the back in terrified shrieks. In unison, the hooded patrons tossed their cloaks aside, revealing the blazing sunburst robes beneath.

Stepping over the splintered threshold, Wen Zhuliu stared down at the boy struggling to drag himself upright from the wreckage, then looked down at his own palm, a flicker of deep contemplation passing through his gaze.

A Wen enforcer planted a heavy boot into the back of Wei Wuxian’s knee, forcing him to crash hard onto both knees.

Wen Chao’s greasy face swam into his line of sight, twisting with cruel, manic glee. "Down already?! Weren't you dancing around like a madman back in the Xuanwu cave? One hit and you're eating dirt?! Hahaha! Go on, dance for me now! Keep acting tough!"

Wang Lingjiao’s shrill, impatient voice piped up from the doorway: "Wen-gongzi, chop off his hand! He still owes us an arm!"

"No, no, no, what's the rush?" Wen Chao grinned. "We spent ages hunting this little rat down. Chopping his hand off will cause too much bleeding; if he dies too fast, the fun is ruined. Melt his core first! I want to hear him scream his lungs out just like that little bastard Jiang Cheng!"

Wang Lingjiao purred, "Melt his core first, then take the hand!"

Listening to them plan his execution with such cheerful malice, Wei Wuxian spat a mouthful of dark blood and laughed. "Come on, then! Bring out whatever torture you've got!"

Wang Lingjiao smiled sweetly. "You asked for it!"

Wen Chao sneered, "Still playing the hero with one foot in the grave!"

Wei Wuxian’s lips curved into a cold, chilling smirk. "It'sbecauseI have one foot in the grave that I'm thrilled! I was terrified you wouldn't finish the job. Torture me to death if you have the guts! The more brutal, the better! The moment I die, I'll return as a vicious, malevolent wraith, haunting every last dog of the Qishan Wen Clan day and night, cursing your entire bloodline!"

Wen Chao’s laugh hitched in his throat.

Noble heirs from prestigious bloodlines—like Jiang Fengmian and Madam Yu—had been steeped in sacred arrays and ancestral wards since birth, undergoing countless Soul-Calming Rites throughout their lives, making it near impossible for them to transform into vengeful spirits upon death. But Wei Wuxian was different. He was the son of a servant, brought into Lotus Pier late in boyhood, completely untouched by those sacred binding ceremonies. If he died choking on monstrous resentment, his unyielding soul would indeed become an absolute nightmare to exorcise. And the more horrific and prolonged his torture was in life, the more savage and unstoppable the resulting wraith would be.

Sensing his hesitation, Wang Lingjiao chimed in hastily, "Wen-gongzi, don't listen to his bluffing! Becoming a fierce ghost requires celestial alignment, geographical harmony, and karmic convergence—miss one, and you're just scattered ash! Even if he does turn, could the mighty Qishan Wen Clan truly fail to crush a stray ghost? We tracked him down to make him pay; are we really going to spare him over a few cheap threats?"

Wen Chao snapped back to reality. "Of course not!"

Knowing he was doomed, a profound, eerie calm settled over Wei Wuxian’s mind. His bone-deep hatred hardened into an unyielding, razor-sharp resolve. Seeing that tranquil, unblinking glare, Wen Chao felt an uneasy chill prickle across his scalp. Masking it with fury, he kicked Wei Wuxian square in the gut. "Still putting on airs?! Who are you trying to intimidate?! Playing the tough guy?!"

A mob of disciples swarmed in, raining boots and fists upon him. Only when his arms grew tired did Wen Chao call them off: "Enough!"

Coughing up another clot of crimson, a dark, manic thrill buzzed through Wei Wuxian’s marrow.Time for the killing blow? Dying isn't any worse than living through this—at least there's a solid thirty percent chance I come back to tear their throats out!

Wen Chao leaned down, his grin widening into a grotesque smirk. "Wei Ying... do you honestly think you're fearless? Some grand, untouchable hero?"

Wei Wuxian blinked in mock wonder. "My, my. Even a Wen dog can string a coherent sentence together?"

Wen Chao’s fist crashed down across his jaw. "Keep running that mouth," he snarled. "Let's see just how long this heroic backbone of yours lasts!"

He barked an order, and Wen Zhuliu stepped forward, hauling Wei Wuxian off the floorboards by his collar. Straining his neck, Wei Wuxian stared into the dead, impassive eyes of the executioner who had butchered Jiang Fengmian and Madam Yu, burning every line of that face into his soul.

Drawing their spiritual blades, the Wen entourage took to the sky. As the mountain peaks receded into tiny specks beneath their boots, Wei Wuxian’s heart sank:When Jiang Cheng comes down, he won't find a trace of me... Why fly this high? Taking me up here just to throw me to the dirt?

After a long flight, a jagged, pitch-black mountain suddenly tore through the pure white sea of clouds.

The peak radiated an oppressive, suffocating miasma of pure death—like a gargantuan, ancient corpse that had rotted for thousands of years, striking dread into the soul from miles away.

Wen Chao brought his sword to a halt right above the abyss. "Wei Ying, do you know what this place is?"

He let out a raspy, cackling laugh. "This place... is called the Burial Mounds."

The name sent an icy shiver rocketing up Wei Wuxian’s spine.

Wen Chao grinned, watching him squirm. "The Burial Mounds sit right here in Yiling; growing up in Yunmeng, you must have heard the legends. A mountain of corpses. An ancient battlefield. Pick any random patch of dirt on that peak, dig a single shovel down, and you'll unearth a skeleton. Every unclaimed corpse in the region gets rolled into a straw mat and tossed down there."

The formation descended slightly, skimming the churning black fog.

"Look at that dark resentful energy," Wen Chao purred. "Heavy, isn't it? Thick with malice? Even our Wen Clan has no way to cleanse it—we could only throw up boundary wards to keep people out. And this is daytime. Come nightfall, every nightmare imaginable crawls out of the earth. A living man stepping foot in there loses body and soul alike—swallowed whole, with no return, never to walk out again."

He seized Wei Wuxian by the hair, dragging his face upward, his voice dropping into a venomous whisper:

"And you... will never walk out again, either!"

With a vicious shove, he hurled Wei Wuxian into the abyss.

"Aaaaaaagh—!!!"
